answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (report.py, read-only; no PBS jobs, no hazard.py):

Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window).
Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849, of which 34 are above the catalogue completeness magnitude Mc.
Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — LBNL catalogue magnitudes) — Sigma and P(Mw>=5.5) per year for each b scenario:
  b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198 (P(M>=5.5) over observed volume = 5.236e-06), P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922  (observed-volume P(M>=5.5) = 0.0002155), P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474   (observed-volume P(M>=5.5) = 0.0006484), P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Which is which: the calibrated probability is the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue-based result (Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5) — the per-b Sigma and P(Mw>=5.5)/yr values above, which use catalogue magnitudes ML -0.48 to 0.07. The DAS-based number (b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842) is an upper bound only: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and every detection is counted as an event at or above Mc, so it over-counts and must not be read as a calibrated hazard probability. Under the calibrated catalogue result, a Pohang-like Mw >= 5.5 event is very unlikely (P/yr from ~1.2e-04 at b=1.0 up to ~1.5e-02 at b=0.65); the DAS upper bound (0.07842/yr) is substantially higher but not calibrated.
